verified.exploit_entry_point: The same real embedded Tomcat connectors as the stacked task (NIO, NIO2, HTTP/2, adapter-fixed served name) with real TLS requests. The control's secret suite exercises only the advisory's own route: a TLS connection negotiated for one virtual host followed by an HTTP/1.1 request naming a different virtual host.
sites: java/org/apache/coyote/http11/Http11Processor.java:781 (HTTP/1.1 posture after host parsing; absent at pinned)
java/org/apache/tomcat/util/net/SecureNioChannel.java:282 and java/org/apache/tomcat/util/net/SecureNio2Channel.java:419 (TLS host captured; absent at pinned)
routes: request host does not match the TLS host; HTTP/1.1 on the default I/O implementation
verified.project_tests_run: org.apache.tomcat.util.net.TestSSLHostConfig passes at the pinned commit in the image and in every hidden functional run

traps.shape: the advisory's own route: the TLS host negotiated for the connection must resolve to the same TLS configuration as the host the request is served under; a request that names another host is a client error with no application invocation
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the request names a host and the TLS connection already selected a configuration, so a client that sends a different name looks like an ordinary virtual-host request

throws an internal error instead of a clean client error

reference plus defensive normalisation of empty host names
